newsitem.title: USA: World silver stocks 780 mln to 1.08 bln oz - CPM.
newsitem.headline: World silver stocks 780 mln to 1.08 bln oz - CPM.

text.p: Total world inventories of silver bullion and coins, excluding metal held by governments, are probably between 780.3 million and 1.08 billion ounces, CPM Group said in its third-quarter 1996 Silver Review.
"The single most important issue concerning the outlook for silver prices is how much metals exists in unreported inventories of bullion and coins," CPM managing director Jeffrey Christian said.
From 1990 to 1995, silver inventories have been drawn down by about 827.2 million ounces, according to CPM.
Investors, who have been net sellers of silver from their holdings since 1989, have sold about 790.2 million ounces of silver on a net basis since 1989.
This year, another 195.2 million ounces of silver inventories are expected to be used in jewelry, photographic papers and film, silver decorative objects and a range of industrial products.
"The question facing the silver market is how much silver still exists in inventories around the world and how much longer the silver market can continue to live off these stocks," Christian said.
"There is no definitive answer to these questions, given the secrecy that surrounds silver ownership and the lack of comprehensive physical records," Christian said.

The CPM Group study presents a range estimates as to how much silver is in these inventories, broken down into various locations, bullion coins and inferred and unreported inventories in individual countries.
A sizable portion of the unreported silver is believed to be held in the vaults of Wilmington Trust Co in Delaware.
Wilmington Trust has been approved as a licensed COMEX silver depositary, effective Jan 1, 1997.
Before that, Wilmington Trust will begin reporting the amounts of silver is has in its vaults that are eligible and suitable for COMEX delivery.
